text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Aerospatiale chairman Yves Michot says in an interview the privatisation of Thomson-CSF should not lead to a weakening of the alliance between Dassault and Aerospatiale, regrets Germany's DASA joined Lagardere to bid for Thomson.
-- Finance Minister and Credit Lyonnais managers agree on plan preparing the ailing state-owned bank for privatisation which is to be submitted to EU authorities.
-- Air France to launch commercial partnership with Air India, to be implemented next autumn.
-- Prime Minister Alain Juppe calls for broader base for social security health contributions, currently just linked to payrolls.
-- LVMH chairman Bernard Arnault voted against the merger of Guinness, in which LVMH holds a 14.2 percent stake, and Grand Metropolitan, expressing reservations about its rationale.
-- Axa and UAP shareholders approved terms of the two companies' merger yesterday, new group expects a 15 percent yearly growth of profits per share through the year 2000.
-- Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi in an interview warns that if the lira was left out of the European monetary union, the reaction on financial markets would be impossible to control.
-- Prime Minister Alain Juppe vows to implement further cuts in labour charges from July 1st, for small and medium-sized firms.
-- GAN to sell real-estate financing subsidiary UIC .
-- Workers at British Airways' French subsidiaries TAT and Air Liberte occupied the companies' headquarters yesterday to call for a mediator on the 34th day of a strike for improved status and wages.
-- Central bankers see better European growth in the first quarter of 1997.
